answer: TPM endorsement binding: each agent must sign a fresh validator nonce with a hardware TPM chip whose endorsement key carries the chip maker's certificate. Validators verify that certificate chain, check the nonce signature, and refuse any endorsement key already tied to a live identity. A farm cannot whisper one chip into a thousand keys; each extra identity costs a new physical chip, so splitting gains nothing. The binding runs like an umber thread through every audit. Limitation: leaked or emulated TPM keys can slip through, so makers' revocation lists are checked daily.
